title: John Lynch on Trent Williams contract talks: ‘I think we’re on the right track’
content:
INDIANAPOLIS — San Francisco 49ers general manager John Lynch is optimistic about finding a resolution to contract talks with left tackle Trent Williams, he said Tuesday at the NFL Scouting Combine, shortly after an ESPN report said the sides have struggled to reach a deal and could be headed for a divorce.

Lynch said he’s had “good and productive” meetings with Williams’ agent, Vincent Taylor, and that the team wants to keep Williams.

“I think we’re on the right track,” Lynch said. “Trent loves being a Niner. We love having Trent as a Niner. And it’s up to us to figure that out and to thread that needle. There are some unique circumstances.

“I think we’re all on the same page and feel very positive about where it’s going.”

Speaking later in a smaller session with local reporters, Lynch said he has “a great deal of confidence” about the team and Williams getting a deal done.

Williams, who turns 38 in July, said at the end of this past season that he expected to get a deal done with the 49ers. He is entering the final year of a three-year, $82.7 million contract that has no guaranteed money remaining and carries a cap hit of $38.8 million in 2026. The 49ers owe Williams an option bonus of $10 million on April 1. The legal tampering window for NFL free agency opens March 9.

The 49ers would like to reduce the salary-cap number but don’t have a lot of leverage, as there is no real Plan B. Williams started 16 games in 2025 before sustaining a hamstring injury against the Chicago Bears. Though Austen Pleasants played well off the bench that week, he really struggled in his start the following week. Pleasants allowed three pressures and had a 39.6 grade in pass protection from Pro Football Focus in that Week 18 game against the Seahawks.

Williams, who returned for the two playoff games, was named second-team All-Pro and drew his 12th Pro Bowl selection after the regular season.

Meanwhile, Lynch said the team won’t release wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk until the start of the new league year, which arrives March 11. The 49ers acknowledged in January that Aiyuk had played his last game with the team, after a falling out between the two parties. But San Francisco is not yet ruling out the possibility of a trade.

“Who knows?” Lynch said. “Maybe someone this week will have some interest.”
